questions.question: Explain what a rubric is and why it is used, show how the crane's specifications become criteria with point levels, and describe how level descriptions should be written.
questions.expected_answer: A rubric is a scoring table with criteria down the side, levels of achievement with points across the top and in each cell a description of what that level looks like, so that every model is judged against the same statements and receives the same score whoever evaluates. Criteria come from the specifications: lifting ten clips or the washer scores three down to zero for none; releasing all within one second three down to none zero; sorting with no non-ferrous pieces three, one piece two, two pieces one, more zero; reach of 150 millimetres lift and 200 millimetres move three, one of the two met two; stability through three tests three, back lifts but stands two, must be held one, falls zero; indicator bulb two or zero; plus three-point criteria for the drawing matching the model and the flow chart followed, totalling twenty-two. Descriptions must be observable, such as the back edge never lifting during three tests rather than good stability, and the rubric is agreed by the class before testing.

questions.question: Describe how a team evaluates another team's crane objectively and fairly, and how feedback is written and received.
questions.expected_answer: The evaluating team runs the tests itself with the rubric, dish and ruler: lowering and lifting the magnet, counting clips lifted and retained after release, measuring height and move, watching the base's back edge and checking what crossed, for three runs, scoring each criterion from the observed level rather than effort or appearance. Fairness requires every crane to be tested the same way with the same dish and height, the owners pressing their own switch, no helping or hindering, a jammed run noted and restarted, scoring only what was seen, disagreements settled by the rubric's words, and signed sheets. Feedback below the scores gives about three things that worked with reasons and three improvements with reasons and suggestions, strength first. Teams receive their own sheets, ask about anything unclear and keep them for the written evaluation, and the class compares scores to sharpen any vague cells.

questions.question: Set out the structure of the team presentation and the three explanations it must contain, and say how evidence is used during it.
questions.expected_answer: Four minutes with every member speaking, in design-process order: the brief and the dealer's need; the investigation evidence on magnets, metals and crane pictures; both sketches and the reason for the choice, then the working drawing and circuit diagram; the flow chart and what took longer in making; test results against the specifications including failures and fixes; one live lift from pile to bin; and improvements. It must explain that only ferrous metals are attracted because their domains align in the field while copper, brass and aluminium are not, so switching off releases the steel into the bin; that the electromagnet is strengthened by more turns, more current with the caution of heat, a thicker or longer soft iron core and sound insulation; and that recycling saves ore, energy and water, keeps metal from landfill and gives gleaners a living, unlike theft of cable and manhole covers. Evidence is held up as each stage is mentioned, numbers are read from the table, and a failed demonstration is diagnosed calmly.
